subject: Streaming metrics & contract language request — measurement, exclusions, remediation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@finnova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + clarifications from today — streaming latency, concurrency, next steps

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put a measurement definition into a draft SLA for your legal and procurement teams. I copied Marissa (SE) to help with the technical wording.

What I captured from the conversation:
- Primary requirement: live audio->text streaming where the application expects incremental tokens with tail latency sensitivity. You mentioned 95th percentile tail targets.
- Target numbers you gave: 95th percentile tail latency target ~150 ms per token (for final token arrival), peak concurrent live sessions ~200, sustained request-rate equivalent ~80 request/s at our front door (average mixture of short and medium sequences).
- You also called out that spikes during full-system maintenance windows are acceptable if we call them out as exclusions.

Clarifying asks (so Marissa and I can draft precise measurement language):
1) For the 95th percentile latency target do you mean per-token generation latency measured at Redwood's API edge, or end-to-end (client -> Redwood -> client)?
2) Can you confirm the expected session/session-length distribution? You mentioned many short sessions (~2–6s) and ~10% long sessions (30–90s).
3) Any regulatory constraints for reporting cadence (e.g., weekly report vs monthly), and who receives it? Procurement usually wants monthly summarized metrics + incident-level notifications.

Next steps:
- Marissa will propose concrete measurement definitions and an initial exclusion list (maintenance windows, upstream network outages, customer-side throttling).
- Ben will assemble a first-pass SLA paragraph set and send for your review by end of day tomorrow.
- If Finnova legal wants specific credit/remedy language we can surface standard and premium tiers.

Attachments: I will include our measurement spec draft in the follow-up.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment stub: finnova_call_notes.txt)

From: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@finnova.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@finnova.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + clarifications from today — streaming latency, concurrency, next steps

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming and adding detail so your SLA draft can be concrete:

Confirmed numbers:
- Tail latency: 95th percentile per-token arrival as seen by Finnova clients should be <= 150 ms. We can tolerate 99th percentile up to 300 ms for brief windows.
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent live sessions is the baseline for Day 1; please size for 300 burst.
- Throughput: sustained equivalent of 80 req/s, with token-rate variance (short chats vs longer streams) — I'll attach our call log and expected session distribution.

Measurement notes (our preference):
- Measurement point: we prefer Redwood to specify latency measured at Redwood's public API endpoint (server-side), provided you include a defined network hop allowance. If possible, include an optional clause to map to end-to-end in a later addendum.
- Exclusions we expect: force majeure, scheduled maintenance with 48h notice, third-party provider outages (e.g., our cloud provider), and customer-originated denial conditions (client misconfiguration causing massive fanout).
- Reporting cadence: monthly SLA report with 7x24 incident alerts for major outages; please include a weekly synthetic-run summary during the pilot.
- Remedies: we prefer dollar-based service credits rather than rollback clauses; please propose a simple credits table (small/medium/major SLA breaches) in your draft.

Attaching Finnova expected session distribution and an internal doc. Please send the Redwood wording for: (A) exact latency measurement definition, (B) exclusion clause language, (C) remediation/credits table.

Thanks —
Alyssa Morgan
Head of ML Product, Finnova
(Attachments: finnova_streaming_requirements.xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@finnova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Draft measurement/ exclusions/ remedies — attached (redwood_sla_measurement_v1.pdf)

Alyssa —

Attached is a first-pass draft (redwood_sla_measurement_v1.pdf) that addresses the three items you asked for: measurement point, enumerated exclusions, and a simple credits table. High-level summary below — Marissa and Karthik are copied for technical and legal alignment.

1) Latency measurement definition (proposed):
- Measurement point: server-side at Redwood API ingress (Post-TLS termination), timestamped when request is received and when token batch is sent to client via the streaming response.
- Unit: per-token latency measured in milliseconds.
- Percentile calculation window: rolling 30-day window for formal SLA calculations; 95th percentile computed over production traffic that passes validation filters (see exclusions).
- Notes: we include an optional additive allowance of up to 20 ms to account for public Internet variability if Finnova requests end-to-end mapping.

2) Exclusions (proposed):
- Scheduled maintenance windows (48+ hours notice), emergency maintenance announced within our incident channel, force majeure events, third-party provider outages (network, GPU cloud) verified via provider status pages.
- Customer-caused conditions: malformed client requests, credential/tenant misconfiguration, or client-side DDoS (we'll provide a diagnostic report).
- Sampling/validation: traffic failing checksum or authentication will be excluded from percentile calculations.

3) Reporting cadence & format:
- Weekly automated synthetic-run summary during pilot (CSV + charts).
- Monthly SLA report with percentile tables, incident timeline, and remediation actions.
- On-demand drill-down available via the Redwood Console (we'll share controlled access).

4) Remedies (credits table, proposed):
- Minor breach (monthly 95th latency between 150–250 ms): 5% service credit for affected month.
- Major breach (monthly 95th latency >250 ms OR sustained outage >2 hours): 15% credit.
- Severe breach (monthly 95th latency >350 ms OR outage >6 hours): 40% credit + executive review.
- Credit caps and cumulative limits noted in doc.

Open items for your team:
- Acceptable percentile window (we used rolling 30 days; Finnova procurement often asks for calendar-month enforcement).
- Whether you want credits computed pro-rata on impacted routes vs account-level.
- Any specifics on audit access (SOC 2 logs vs ad-hoc exports).

Next steps:
- Marissa: please review measurement wording and confirm operational feasibility for synthetic testing at our scale.
- Ben: will convert the PDF into a redline-ready paragraph that legal can drop into the master agreement (ETA EOD tomorrow).
- Alyssa/Tom: any initial feedback on the credits table would be helpful.

Attachment: redwood_sla_measurement_v1.pdf (Attachment stub: 48KB)

Best —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@finnova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft measurement/ exclusions/ remedies — quick ops clarifications

Alyssa / Ben — quick operational notes from the SE side to make sure the language maps to what we can measure reliably:

- Synthetic vs production measurement: we can run high-fidelity synthetics that mirror Finnova's session distribution (Marissa to own test harness). For formal SLA numbers, we should base on production traffic with the validation filters Ben listed.
- Percentile computation: 95th on per-token latency is straightforward, but we recommend adding a short description of how we group tokens into requests when variable batch sizes are used.
- Concurrency measurement: we measure "active streams" as open websocket/streaming connections with at least one token exchanged in the last 10s. We'll include a probe to capture burst concurrency for the pilot weeks.
- Reporting: we can push a monthly CSV export to your shared Drive folder and provide a weekly summary via a private Redwood Console link.

Ops ask: please confirm the month type (calendar month vs rolling 30-day) and whether Finnova wants per-route or aggregated account-level credits. That drives how we compute and present the data.

I'll prepare a short appendix for the SLA draft that defines the measurement method details (timestamp semantics, aggregation window, excluded classes). Ben — I can deliver that by EOD tomorrow.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment stub: redwood_sla_measurement_appendix_draft.docx)
